| `TY2004` | A handler source is not a regular UTF-8 file of at most 1 MiB in the project, has a string or comment that is not closed, or a direct handler wrote an answer that is not one JSON object with a valid HTTP status. | Project folders and roles / Yon: every language implementation |
| `TY2005` | The server cannot send a request to a handler: the request frame is larger than 16 MiB, does not fit Handler Protocol v1, or the API reference cannot be written. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2006` | A name in the environment allowlist `server.environment` is not valid: use letters, digits and underscores, and start with a letter or an underscore. `ty handler invoke` also uses it for a stream answer, which it cannot show: request the method over HTTP with `ty preview` or `ty start`. | Isolation and security / Environment variables for handlers |
| `TY2007` | The resource limits of the handler supervisor are not valid. A deadline is 1 to 300 seconds, the concurrency and log limits are positive, and the grace time after a cancel is at most 5 seconds. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2010` | The server configuration is not valid, for example a `server.environment` entry that is `*` or names a variable of `ty` itself (`TAC_*`, `TACHYON_*`, `YON_*`, proxy variables), or the firecracker isolation mode does not allow gateways. The message names the entry, never a value. | Isolation and security / Environment variables for handlers; Preview and build / When the project has a problem |
| `TY2015` | A Yon class cannot be used as written, and the message names the rule. `StreamRoute` is used in a language that cannot stream (Java, Groovy or Rust), or a Go stream method returns something other than `iter.Seq[Model]` or `iter.Seq2[Model, error]`. A `Needs` field names a type that no provider declares ("Unresolved dependency"). A Lua class uses a resource that Lua does not support yet: `DataSource`, `RedisTemplate`, a gateway client or `relay`, and in a Lua Tac service a `FilePicker` or `WindowControls` field (ADR 0085). In a Ruby or Lua Tac service it also stops a `Needs` field whose type is another service, which the page would leave nil (ADR 0054, ADR 0085). Tac Lua accepts pure Converter and Convert mapping but refuses other behavior annotations. In F#, it stops a `[<Needs>]` that is not on a settable `member val` with a written type, a type that takes the same role twice (as a primary constructor parameter and as a Needs property, or as two Needs properties), and a type that lists fields in NeedsAll, which F# does not support yet. It also stops a route whose parameter, result or model field names a type that is not a model; a Go `*http.Request`, `context.Context` or multipart file in a model is not JSON data, so read it from the `*http.Request` parameter instead, while other Go package types such as `json.RawMessage` are open JSON values. | Streams / Streaming: Yon; The Yon languages / Languages Yon runs; Dependency injection / A service that needs another service: Tac |
| `TY2020` | A test case failed. `ty preview` still starts and shows the failure in its error box, even if every public method was called. | Test units / Test units |
| `TY2021` | The command cannot find the project folder. Pass a folder that exists, or run the command inside the project. | Install / Install |
| `TY2022` | `ty test --coverage` found a public method of an annotated class that no test case called. | Test units / Test units |
| `TY2023` | No test case called a public method of an annotated class, for example `no test case called GreetingService.message`. `ty preview` starts and lists the methods in its error box. | Test units / Test units |
| `TY2024` | `ty test` or the automatic tests before `ty preview` cannot write or invalidate the record of called methods in `.tachyon/coverage`. | Test units / Test units |

Handler processes and server resources (`TY2101` to `TY2160`):

| Code | What it means | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TY2101` | Role files cannot be read together, or a handler process cannot start. For role files, the message names the problem: a role folder is a symbolic link, there are more than 512 role files or deeper than 32 folders, a role file moves imports or uses a relative import or `require`, two files declare the same type, classes build each other while they load, or an old module manifest is still there. For handlers, the language runtime cannot start or stopped taking work; check that it is installed. | Project folders and roles / Roles decide the folder, modifiers do not; Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2102` | A handler answered with something that is not a valid Handler Protocol v1 answer: the frame is not UTF-8, it ended too early, extra data followed it, or it does not match the request. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2103` | A handler answer is larger than 16 MiB, the most that one frame may hold. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2104` | A handler process crashed or exited with an error. Fix the crash; the next request starts a clean process. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2107` | A handler wrote more log text to stderr than its limit allows, the log could not be read, or a stream or socket handler failed in the middle. Write less log text, or fix the handler. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2110` | A handler did not finish before its deadline. This also happens when all process slots stay busy until the deadline passes: then the process never starts. Make the handler faster, or give it a larger deadline. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2111` | A handler request was cancelled, for example because the caller closed the connection. The server answers `499`. | Modules and lifecycle / Process lifecycle |
| `TY2112` | A program that the server needs is missing when it starts: a program that a gateway calls, or a compiler or runtime for a handler language, such as `rustc`, `kotlinc`, `groovyc`, `dart` or `dotnet`. Install it on `PATH`, or remove the handler that needs it. | Relays and gateways / Calling a method in another language; The Yon languages / Languages Yon runs |
| `TY2160` | A managed storage command failed or was refused: a bad command, a deadline, a FYLO collection name outside its grammar (such as `../etc` or `hd_events`), a FYLO document or queue command on a SQL datasource, or an expired scroll cursor. | Server data / FYLO documents and queue, in every Yon language |

Errors inside a language runner, sent in the answer (`TY2201` to `TY2204`):

| Code | What it means | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TY2201` | A handler raised an error while it ran. The answer carries this code and a safe message, not the details of the error. | Request IDs and error reports / Request IDs and error reports |
| `TY2202` | A handler has no method for the request: no method for this HTTP method (`405`), no topic listeners (`404`), or a middleware without the phase that the server calls. | Request IDs and error reports / Request IDs and error reports |
| `TY2203` | A handler answer or event cannot be written as JSON, or an event is larger than its limit. | Request IDs and error reports / Request IDs and error reports |
| `TY2204` | A stream handler failed after it began to send. The stream ends with this fixed error message, and the details stay in the server log. | Streams / Streaming: Yon |

sections.heading: Codes at run time
sections.body:
A running page can get a code that does not start with `TY`. A client in `client/remotes` fails with an `HTTP_` code, `CANCELLED` or `DEADLINE`, and a native app answers a page with a `TY_NATIVE_` code. Your service code can read the code and show a message.

| Code | What it means | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HTTP_REQUEST` | The request is not valid: larger than 64 KiB with its path, query, headers and body, a method or setting that the transport does not accept, or its deadline passed. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_ORIGIN` | The request goes to another origin than the page, or the server answered with a redirect. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_HEADER` | A header is not allowed: `Cookie`, `Host`, `Origin`, `Referer`, `Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, a name that starts with `Sec-` or `Proxy-`, a bad name or value, or more than 128 headers. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_QUERY` | A query value is not text, a number or a boolean, it is too long, or the whole address is longer than 8 KiB. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_BODY` | A `GET` or `HEAD` request has a body. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_LIMIT` | The answer is larger than 1 MiB, or than the limit that the request set. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_CAPACITY` | The page already has 64 requests waiting. Wait for one to finish. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_STATUS` | The server answered with an error status. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_RESPONSE` | The answer is not JSON or does not have the shape of the model, or a JSON value in the request or the answer is nested deeper than 32 levels or holds a number that JavaScript cannot keep exactly. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_NETWORK` | The browser could not reach the server, or the request failed for another reason. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `HTTP_MISSING` | The client has no HTTP transport. The default transport runs only in the browser, so give the client an HTTP adapter in its Setup, for example in a test. | Calling the server from a page / Rust awaits a real Yon endpoint |
| `HTTP_ARGUMENT` | A request method got an argument that does not fit its place in the path, the query or the body. | Calling the server from a page / Client classes that call the server |
| `HTTP_PATH` | The path that a request method builds is not a safe path on the page's origin. | Calling the server from a page / Client classes that call the server |
| `CANCELLED` | The request was cancelled, for example because the component that started it was removed. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `DEADLINE` | The request did not finish within its deadline, at most 60 seconds. | Calling the server from a page / What the browser transport allows |
| `TY_NATIVE_SERVICE` | A page asked a native app for a service that the app does not have. | Rust, Go and C# in the browser / Services are compiled in |
| `TY_NATIVE_REQUIRED` | A native Swift or Kotlin service misses a property that it needs, or the page passed a value of the wrong type. | Rust, Go and C# in the browser / Services are compiled in |
| `TY_NATIVE_OWNER` | The page that asked is gone or was replaced, so the native app refuses the call. | Rust, Go and C# in the browser / Services are compiled in |
| `TY_NATIVE_ROUTE` | A call from the page to a native service did not say which page it came from. | Rust, Go and C# in the browser / Services are compiled in |

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.summary: Short meanings of the words that the guides use.

sections.heading: Words
sections.body:
Each word below is explained where the guides first use it. This list keeps the short meanings in one place.

| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Abstract member | In F#, a member written with `abstract` and no body, as in `abstract findByStatus: status: BehaviorJSON -> Task<BehaviorJSON>`. When it holds Query, Convert, Gateway or a request annotation, Tachyon writes its body during the build. |
| Access rule | The annotation that says who may call a route: `@Public`, `@SignedIn` or `@Allow(Role)`. A route without one stops the build with `TY1322`. |
| Accessible name | The text that a screen reader says for a button, link or field: the text inside it, its `aria-label`, the element that `aria-labelledby` names, or its `<label>`. Without one, the build stops with `TY1336`. |
| Annotation | A marker on a class, a field or a method, such as `@Service`. It tells Tachyon what to do. |
| API baseline | The API of the last release, saved by `ty api freeze` in `server/api-baseline.json`. A later build that breaks it without a new major version stops with `TY1338`. |
| Application service | A Rust service in `client/services/` with `#[Lifetime({"value":"application"})]` in a native macOS, Linux or Windows app. One instance starts with the app, keeps running when pages change (on macOS also when the window closes), and stops once when the app quits. Page services get it by `Arc` injection, and menu actions call its methods. It lives inside the app only; Tachyon never installs a system service or starts it at login. Other builds refuse it with `TY1406`. |
| Assertion | A check in a test case that fails the case when the result is wrong, such as `Assert.equals(1200, total)`, the Python `assert`, the Kotlin `check` or the Swift `precondition`. A test case without one proves nothing (`TY1339`). |
| Binaryen | A set of WebAssembly tools. Its `wasm-opt` program makes a finished WebAssembly module smaller. A release build runs it on Rust, Go, Swift, Kotlin and Java modules when it is installed (see WebAssembly compilers per language). |
| Browser API | A feature of the browser, such as the clock or random numbers. Tachyon gives every Tac service a small set of them, such as `Clock`, `Connectivity` and `Geolocation`, through `@Needs`. |
| Browser API grant | A name in `tac.browserApis` in `client/manifest.json`, such as `clipboard`. `Clipboard`, `Share`, `Notifications` and `Geolocation` work only when the project grants them. |
| Browser interop | Code in another language than JavaScript or TypeScript that calls the browser directly, such as Go's `syscall/js`. Tachyon refuses it in Tac code (`TY1317`). |
| Browser transport | The code that sends the requests of a compiled or Ruby client in `client/remotes` from the page. It has fixed limits, and it fails with a code such as `HTTP_LIMIT` or `HTTP_ORIGIN` (see Error codes, Codes at run time). |
| BrowserFakes | In a Go, Ruby, Lua, Swift, C# or F# test unit, the answers that Tachyon's browser APIs give, because a test unit has no page. `BrowserFakes{}.Answer("clock", "now", 1000)` makes `Clock` answer 1000. |
| Built-in event model | An event model that Tachyon declares for you, such as `ConnectivityChanged` or `PositionFound`. The page publishes it; a listener uses it like any model, without a file in `client/models/`. |
| Bundle | The built files of your app that you publish. `ty bundle` makes them. |
| Class table | In Lua, the one global table of a class file, such as `OrderService = {}`. Its methods are `function OrderService:list()`, and Tachyon makes each object with the table as its metatable (ADR 0085). In a Tac service, each object also starts with its own copy of the table's fields. |
| Cohesion | How closely the code of one method belongs together. In a cohesive service, a public method only coordinates, and each private method does one small job. |
| Component | In a template, a part of a page that you can use again: a folder in `client/components` with a `tac.html` file. The old annotation `Component` is now `Helper` (`TY1308`). |
| Compressed copy | A `.br` (Brotli) or `.gz` (gzip) file that a release build writes next to a script, style, page, data or WebAssembly file. `ty start` sends it to a browser that accepts it, and the browser unpacks it to the same bytes. |
| Content Security Policy | A response header that lists what a page may load and run, such as scripts from other sites or WebAssembly. |
| Contract | A declaration with no implementation, such as a Java `interface`, a Rust `trait`, a Swift `protocol` or a Python `Protocol` class. An `HTTPClient` and a `Store` are contracts: Tachyon generates each request and each query, and a body in them stops the build with `TY1308`. JavaScript, TypeScript and Ruby write a class whose methods have empty bodies instead. |
| Control element | An element of a Tac view that the compiler reads and the browser never sees: `<logic>` for a conditional, `<loop>` for a loop, and `<switch>` with `<case>`. There is no `<if>`, `<else>` or `<for>` element (`TY1367`). |
| Controller | A class in `server/controllers` that answers HTTP requests. |
| Converter | A contract whose Convert methods copy fields from one JSON value into a new one by a literal field plan, like a MapStruct mapper interface. It needs no behavior context, so Tachyon builds it with no constructor argument, and a service or controller asks for it with Needs in Yon and in Tac. |
| Coverage | The public methods of annotated classes that a test case really called while `ty test` ran. A call on a Fake does not count. `ty preview` lists a method that was not called in its error box (`TY2023`), and `ty test --coverage` fails on it. |
| Custom element | A tag that JavaScript defines with `customElements.define`, such as `<shop-counter>`. Its name must contain a hyphen. A component listed in `tac.elements` becomes one, so other apps can use it (`TY1358`). |
| Decision | A place where code chooses a path: `if`, `switch`, a ternary, `&&`, `||`, `??`, `catch`, or a loop. |
| Declaration file | A TypeScript file that ends in `.d.ts` and describes types without any code. The build writes one beside each exported element, so a TypeScript page knows its tag, props and events. |
| Dependency | A class that another class needs, because it names it in a field, a `Needs` list or its code. Dependencies point down, and no chain of them may loop back (`TY1327`). |
| Derived delete | A Store method whose name starts with `deleteBy` (or `delete_by_`). It removes every record that its predicates match and answers how many it removed. |
| DNS rebinding | An attack where a web page points its own name at your computer, so that the browser lets the page read a server on `127.0.0.1` as if it were the page's own. A loopback Tachyon server refuses such a request because its `Host` name is not allowed (`TY1366`). |
| Drag region | An element marked `data-tac-drag-region`. In a native window with an integrated title bar, dragging it moves the window, and a double-click does what the system title bar setting says. Controls inside it, and elements marked `data-tac-no-drag`, keep their clicks. |
| Duplicated code | A block of code that appears twice or more, even with other names or values. Tachyon refuses it with `TY1315`. |
| Embedded Swift | A small form of Swift for tiny devices, without `Codable`, `Any` values and `as?` casts. Tachyon does not use it for Swift services on the web, because services need those parts. |
| Emscripten | A compiler from C and C++ to WebAssembly; its C++ program is `em++`. Tachyon compiles C++ services with it, and builds the mruby and Lua runtimes with it once on your machine. `ty doctor --install` downloads it with emsdk and checks the SHA-256. |
| Environment allowlist | The list `server.environment` in `server/application.json`: the names and prefix patterns, such as `HD_*`, of the variables of `ty`'s environment that handler processes may see. Empty by default; `*` and `ty`'s own variables are refused with `TY2010`. |
| Error box | The box that `ty preview` shows on top of open pages when a build fails: each problem with its code, message, file and line, and help. It has a Dismiss button, and it goes away after the next good build. |
| Error page | The page that `ty preview` serves when the project has a problem at start. It lists the problems and opens the site as soon as the project builds. |
| Event | A message that one service publishes and other services receive. |
| Field | A value that belongs to an object, such as `count` in a service. |
| Field case | The way a language writes the name of a variable or a field: lowerCamel case (`cartStore`) in JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, Go and PHP, snake_case (`cart_store`) in Python, Ruby and Rust, and `_cartStore` for a private C# field. A field that holds an injected class uses it, or the build stops with `TY1332`. |
| FYLO | A document store from fylo.del.ma that ships as one `fylo` binary and keeps one JSON file per document. With the `fylo` datasource driver, DataSource reads and changes documents by id, scrolls through them and runs FYLO's queue (ADR 0032). |
| Generated folder | `.tachyon` in the project and `dist/.tachyon` in the build. Tachyon writes them again when it needs them, so you can delete them at any time. They hold no saved data. |
| Header-only file | A C++ `.hpp` file that holds the whole class, its members and their bodies, with no `.cpp` file beside it. Each C++ Tac class is one header-only file named after the class (ADR 0099). |
| Helper | A class in `client/helpers` or `server/helpers` marked `@Helper`. Services use it for part of their work. Tachyon creates it and gives it to them through `Needs`. See Helpers, utilities and private methods. |
| Identity provider | The one class marked `@IdentityProvider`. Its method `identify` reads the request and says who is signed in and which roles they have. |
| Integrated title bar | A window setting, `"titleBar": "integrated"` in `tac.application.window`, where the page reaches the top edge of a macOS window and the real window buttons sit on it, as one surface. Other platforms keep the standard title bar (ADR 0098). |
| Joint compilation | Compiling Groovy files and Java files in one step, so that each can use the classes of the other. Tachyon compiles a Groovy handler this way with its generated Java runtime. |
| Last good build | The newest build that succeeded. When a save breaks the build, `ty preview` keeps serving it and shows the error box. |
| Layer | A level of the app: entry points (controllers and views), services, helpers, and data access (stores, repositories and clients). A class needs only classes of its own layer or a lower one. |
| Lifecycle hook | A method that runs when an object starts (`OnStart`) or stops (`OnStop`). |
| Localhost name | `localhost` or a name that ends in `.localhost`, such as `shop.localhost`. Browsers and Tachyon send it to your own computer (loopback) without asking DNS. `ty preview --host shop.localhost` serves the app there, a loopback server always answers it, and `outgoing.hosts` may list it for Yon code (ADR 0094). |
| Lua web runtime | Tachyon's Lua 5.4 interpreter, compiled to WebAssembly. Your machine builds it once from the pinned lua.org source with Emscripten, into the Tachyon cache, and every Tac Lua service of a page runs on it (ADR 0085). |
| LuaCATS | The type comments that the Lua language server reads, such as `---@param id integer`, `---@return Order[]` and `---@class Order` with `---@field name string`. Lua writes every type of a class this way (`TY1356`). |
| Magic value | A text or number written in the code without a name, used twice, or a number in a condition. Tachyon asks for a class constant instead (`TY1330`). |
| Menu action | A native menu item whose `action` calls a method of an application service instead of opening a page. The page keeps its state. The service can forward an event to the page with `CurrentPageEvents` (ADR 0097). |
| Middleware | Code that runs before every request and after every response. |
| Model | A data type that describes the shape of a value, such as a product. It lives in `client/models` or `server/models`, one model in each file, and the file is named after it. In every Tac language, a service field, a list field and a method argument can hold a model, and a model can hold other models. |
| mruby | A small Ruby interpreter. Tachyon builds a pinned mruby once on your machine with Ruby and Emscripten, and every Ruby Tac service of a page runs on it as WebAssembly (ADR 0054). |
| Native Go package | A plain Go package with its own package name, such as a git client or a spec package. It lives in the Go module in `server/packages/`, whose `go.mod` names the module, and role files import it by module path. It is not a role, so it needs no marker and the class-file rules do not apply (ADR 0095). |
| Native host | The desktop or mobile app that Tachyon builds for a target. |
| Needs property | In F#, a settable property marked `[<Needs>]`, as in `[<Needs>] member val OrderStore : OrderStore = Unchecked.defaultof<OrderStore> with get, set`. Tachyon sets it right after the primary constructor runs, like a Spring field, and `[<Named("...")>]` chooses another provider. A type may not take one role both as a constructor parameter and as a Needs property (`TY2015`). |
| Page | A `tac.html` file under `client/pages`. Its folder decides its URL. |
| Plain state | A field with a starting value, such as `count = 0`. Tachyon never fills it, and it may stay empty. |
| Primary constructor | In F#, the parameter list written right after the type name, as in `type OrderService(orderStore: OrderStore) =`. Tachyon fills these parameters with the roles they name, so an F# type takes its dependencies, its `DataSource` and its `ApplicationEventPublisher` there. It is the recommended form; a Needs property is the other one. `[<NeedsAll>]` on the type states this; in a Tac service it also makes the parameters take the component's properties, as in `type SnippetService(files: string list) =` (ADR 0073). |
| Private member | A method or field that only its own class uses. Each language has its own private form, such as `private` or a name that starts with `_`. A member stays public only when a view, another class or Tachyon uses it (`TY1333`). |
| Public read | A `Cached` GET that a JavaScript or TypeScript `HTTPClient` sends without credentials and without `no-store`, so the service worker may answer it by the `tac.cache` rules of its path (ADR 0087). |
| Pyodide | CPython compiled to WebAssembly. A Python Tac service runs on the pinned Pyodide 314.0.7 (CPython 3.14.2). You copy its five core files into the Tachyon cache; `ty` checks the size and SHA-256 of each file and never downloads Python (`TY1605`, ADR 0093). |
| Queue delivery | One message that `claim` hands to a worker, with its `id`, `receipt`, `attempt` and `payload`. The worker finishes it with `ack` or gives it back with `nack`; a delivery that is not acknowledged before its lease ends is claimed again. |
| Realm | One side of the app. Tac is the frontend realm, and Yon is the backend realm. A file never imports a file of the other realm (`TY1369`). |
| Repository | The base that a Store can extend, like Spring Data's `CrudRepository`: `Repository<Entity, Id>` gives the store `findById`, `findAll`, `save` and `deleteById` without declaring them. |
| Required field | A field that Tachyon fills before any method runs: a `Needs` field, or a `NeedsAll` field without a starting value. It is never null, so it uses the language's non-null form, such as `name!: string` or `late final String name;`. A nullable one stops the build with `TY1331`. |
| Role | The job of a class, such as service, controller or store. The role decides the folder of the file. |
| Route | A path and an HTTP verb that a controller method answers, such as GET /products. |
| Scroll cursor | The opaque text that one `scroll` page answers as `nextCursor`. Pass it to read the next page; it lasts 15 minutes in the server that made it, and null means the last page. |
| Secret | A value that gives access, such as a password, a token or a key. It lives in `.env`, never in the code (`TY1324`). |
| Service | In Tac, a class in `client/services` that holds the data and the actions of a view. In Yon, a class in `server/services` that controllers use. |
| Setup | The class that gives named adapters (caches, HTTP, entities and the authorization hooks) from its `configure` method, like a Spring `@Configuration`. Tachyon configures it once per page in Tac and once per server process in Yon, so every behavior context built from it shares the same adapters. |
| Shadow DOM | A separate tree of elements inside an element. The styles of the page do not reach inside it, except inherited values and CSS custom properties. An exported component draws its view there. |
| Signature | The name of a method and its parameters. A method takes at most 4 parameters (`TY1329`). |
| Simpler form | A way to write the same code that reads more plainly, such as `items.some(isReady)` instead of `items.filter(isReady).length > 0`. `ty preview` and `ty test` show it as a suggestion (`TY1340` to `TY1355`), which never stops the build. |
| Size budget | The most script and WebAssembly that one route may load, in kilobytes as sent (`tac.budgets.script`, `tac.budgets.webassembly`). A route that loads more than one web runtime gets a measured allowance for each runtime after the largest one. Over it, a release build stops with `TY1337`. |
| Slot | A place in a component template where the children of the component show. `<slot>` takes the children without a `slot` attribute; a named slot, such as `<slot name="title">`, takes the children with `slot="title"` (`TY1404`). |
| Socket | A WebSocket: a connection that stays open, so both sides can send messages at any time. |
| SSRF | Server-side request forgery: a caller makes your server send a request to an address that they choose. Tachyon allows only the hosts that you list (`TY1326`). |
| Standard attribute | A C++ marker in double square brackets, such as `[[Service]]` or `[[Needs]]`. Tachyon reads its markers in C++ this way: `class [[Service]] OrderService` puts the class marker after `class`, in PascalCase and without a namespace (`TY1371`). |
| Store | A contract that names an Entity and declares its queries, like a Spring Data repository interface. Tachyon writes each query, and a service asks for the store with Needs in Yon and in Tac. |
| Stream | One HTTP answer that stays open and sends many messages (server-sent events). |
| Structure check | The check of every role folder and file in both realms that runs before a build writes output or starts a compiler. It lists the problems of all files in one run: markers, role names, file names, one class per file, dependencies and imports of the other realm. |
| Style scope | The part of the page that a component's `tac.css` reaches. The compiler wraps the style sheet in CSS `@scope`: it starts at the component and stops at every nested component, so the styles of a parent never change a child. |
| Tac | The frontend part of Tachyon: pages, components and services. |
| Target | The kind of app that you build: web, macos, windows, linux, ios or android. |
| TeaVM | A compiler from Java bytecode to JavaScript and WebAssembly. Tachyon compiles Java web services with its WebAssembly garbage collection (WasmGC) backend; `ty doctor --install` downloads its jars into the Tachyon cache, or `TAC_TEAVM_HOME` names a folder of your own. |
| Test case | A method of a test unit whose name begins with `test`. It prepares values, calls the code and checks the result with `Assert` or the assert of its language, with no branch or loop (`TY1339`). With `ValueSource`, Tachyon runs it once for each input. |
| Test unit | A class whose name ends with `Test`. `ty test` runs it. |
| TinyGo | A Go compiler for small devices and WebAssembly. It leaves out most of the Go runtime, so a Go service module is many times smaller. A release build uses it first for Go web services (`tac.go.compiler`). |
| Title bar insets | The CSS custom properties `--tac-titlebar-height`, `--tac-titlebar-leading-inset` and `--tac-titlebar-trailing-inset`, which the native host sets so that page content stays clear of the window buttons. They are `0px` in full screen and not set in a browser, so write a fallback value. |
| Topic | A model marked `@Topic`. Tachyon saves each published value in the topic log and sends it to the listeners in every Yon language and in open pages. |
| Topic log | The file that keeps the values of one topic, one JSON line each: `data/topics/<name>.jsonl`, or the folder that `topics.directory` in `server/application.json` names. It is saved data, so back it up. |
| Transaction | A group of changes that all happen or all do not happen. AllOrNothing opens one on a service method, and a store that the method calls joins it. |
| Trusted proxy | A reverse proxy listed in `server.proxies` in `server/application.json`, by IP address or CIDR range. `ty` keeps the `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*` and `X-Real-IP` headers only from a trusted proxy; from any other client it replaces them with the real client address (ADR 0096). |
| `ty` | The one program that creates, previews, builds, tests and serves a Tachyon app. |
| Type comment | A comment that a tool reads for the type of a field, parameter or return value, in a language whose syntax has no types: JSDoc `@param {number} amount` in JavaScript, YARD `# @param amount [Integer]` in Ruby and LuaCATS `---@param amount integer` in Lua. It holds a type, never an explanation. Every member of a class has a type (`TY1356`). |
| Utility class | A class in `client/shared/utils` (Tac, nested folders allowed) or `server/utils` (Yon) with only static methods and no state. Code that would repeat lives there, and every class of the realm can call it, so it names no role class (`TY1327`). |
| Vendored Go module | A third-party Go module that `server/packages/go.mod` requires and whose code the app commits in `server/packages/vendor/`, written by `go mod vendor` together with `vendor/modules.txt`. Tachyon builds Go offline with `-mod=vendor` and never downloads a module, so a module that is not vendored fails with `TY1368`. The project rules and the secret and code safety checks skip `vendor/` (ADR 0095). |
| View | The `tac.html` file of a page or a component. |
| WasmGC | WebAssembly with garbage collection: the browser manages the memory of objects. Dart, Kotlin and Java services need it, so they run in Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2 and newer. |
| WebAssembly | A compiled format that browsers run. Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Dart and C++ services use it in the browser. Ruby, Lua and Python services run on an interpreter compiled to it: mruby, Tachyon's Lua runtime and Pyodide. Dart, Kotlin and Java need WasmGC. |
| WebView | The browser view that is built into the operating system. A native host shows your pages in it. |
| WindowControls | The browser API for the native app window: `granted`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `fullscreen`, `close`, `resize` and `setTitle`. A service injects it, and `tac.application.window.controls` grants each control (ADR 0087). |
| Yon | The backend part of Tachyon: controllers, services and stores on the server. |

sections.heading: Words for platform, target and environment
sections.body: platform is the kind of device. The macos, windows and linux targets are the desktop platform. ios and android are the mobile platform. web is the web platform. environment and os mean the same thing: the host that the app really runs on. For native bundles, that is the operating system. For browser bundles, it is web. target names the bundle output. Service language is the language of a Tac service: JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Dart or Ruby, and Lua, Python and C++ with limits (see Choosing a service language).
